job_description.title: Paid Search Manager
job_description.why_this_role_exists: Example Booking Software sells online booking, reminders and payments for salons, clinics, studios and personal trainers. Google Ads is our largest paid channel, and we want it to bring more customers at a cost we can sustain. You will own it.
what_you_will_own_in_year_one: Grow sign-ups from Google Ads by 30% without raising what each one costs.
Halve the spend on searches that never turn into customers within 6 months.
Run at least 2 ad or landing page tests a month and write up what we learned.
job_description.what_you_will_work_with: A five-figure monthly search budget across 5 live campaigns, Google Ads and GA4, and a content lead, a product marketing manager and a web developer.
you_will_need: Has managed Google Ads search budgets across several campaigns and can show what changed because of their work
Reviews search terms every week and turns them into negatives, keywords and ad changes
Sets bids and budgets against a cost-per-result ceiling and can explain the trade-offs
Checks that conversion tracking counts each sign-up once before trusting a number
Writes clear, correct English for ads, test readouts and weekly notes
helpful_not_required: Has run Performance Max campaigns and can explain how they judged its results
Has sold software on monthly plans
Has worked with a landing page builder or a developer on page tests
job_description.pay_and_benefits: $95,000 to $115,000 base salary, plus benefits. Remote, for candidates living in the US.
how_we_hire: Screen, 30 minutes, with the Head of Growth
Outcome deep dive, 60 minutes, with the Head of Growth
Paid take-home, capped at 3 hours, paid $150 whatever the outcome, then a 45-minute review with the product marketing manager
Working with others, 45 minutes, with the content lead
We reply within 5 working days of each stage
job_description.internal_note: Pay range source: the company's own 2026 compensation review, dated 2026-09-15.

questions.q: What made you apply, and what would you want to own in your next role?
follow_ups: What would make you turn this job down?
Our range is $95,000 to $115,000 base, remote in the US. Does that work for you?
questions.strong: Names the kind of account and results they want to own, and is clear on pay and location.
questions.weak: Talks only about the company's brand or perks.

questions.q: Briefly, what is the largest search account you have run on your own, and what did you change in it last month?
follow_ups: How did you decide which search terms to exclude?
How did you check the conversion numbers were right?
questions.strong: Names the budget size, the number of campaigns and one recent change with its result, in a few sentences.
questions.weak: Lists tools and certificates but no account they ran or change they made.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you grew conversions from search without letting cost per conversion rise. What did you change?
follow_ups: What was the cost per conversion before and after?
What did you try that didn't work?
questions.strong: Gives before and after numbers, names the trade-off (volume against cost), and explains how they knew the change caused the result.
questions.weak: Says "we" throughout, gives no numbers, or credits a bid strategy switch alone.

questions.q: In our account a noticeable share of search term spend goes to searches that never convert. How would you work on that in your first month?
follow_ups: How do you decide a search is a negative and not a page problem?
How often would you review search terms?
questions.strong: Separates irrelevant searches from relevant ones that convert poorly, checks a longer window before negating, and sets a weekly rhythm.
questions.weak: Proposes a generic negative list or negates everything with no conversions.

questions.q: How do you check that conversion tracking counts each sign-up once before you trust a number?
follow_ups: What did you find the last time you checked?
What do you do when Google Ads and analytics disagree?
questions.strong: Names concrete checks (counting setting, duplicate actions, a test sign-up) and a time they found a problem.
questions.weak: Assumes the platform number is right.

questions.q: Walk us through your memo. Which action would you take first, and why that one?
follow_ups: Which search did you leave alone on purpose?
How would you know in 2 weeks that it worked?
questions.strong: Defends the order with money at stake and says how they would measure it.
questions.weak: Reads the memo out without explaining the choices.

assesses: working with content and product marketing

questions.q: Tell me about a test you ran with someone outside your team, such as a landing page or offer change. How did you agree on what to test and how to read it?
follow_ups: What happened when the result was flat?
questions.strong: Describes a shared hypothesis, a stopping rule set in advance, and a written readout others used.
questions.weak: Ran tests alone or stopped them when they looked good.

interview_loop.rating: Each interviewer rates the outcomes they own as below bar, at bar or above bar and writes the evidence before the debrief.
interview_loop.decision_rule: Offer only when O1 and O2 are at bar or above across the loop and the take-home scores 70 or more. A strong rating elsewhere never cancels a must-have below bar.

candidate_brief.task: Here are 30 days of search terms from a software company's Google Ads account, with names and numbers disguised. Write a one-page memo: what you would change first, what you would leave alone, and why. List up to 5 actions in order, each with the numbers behind it.
candidate_brief.fine_print: Paid whatever the outcome. The data is disguised and your work is not used in the live account.

findings_a_strong_candidate_catches.finding: Login searches are existing customers, not prospects: add 'login' as a negative on brand and rival campaigns.
Searches for free tools, templates and jobs never sign up: add negatives.
Do not negate a never-converting search that names a customer segment the product serves; fix the ad or landing page instead.
Brand search makes the blended cost per sign-up look better than it is: $12.24 on brand vs $73.36 on everything else.
Rival names has the highest non-brand cost per sign-up ($143.00); check its queries and landing page before adding budget.

answer_key.never_converting_rule: 0 sign-ups and cost above the file's average cost per sign-up ($52.82)
